title: Taoism and Confucianism
examples: What do yin and yang mean?

explain.say: Two great traditions grew in ancient China about 2,500 years ago. Taoism looks to the Tao, the way of nature, and Confucianism looks to good relationships and a well ordered society.

draw.text: Two ways of harmony from ancient China

explain.say: Taoism is linked to the sage Laozi and the short book called the Tao Te Ching. The Tao is the way, the source and flow of everything, so deep that words cannot fully name it.

draw.text: Like water: soft, yet it shapes stone

explain.say: Taoists value wu wei, acting naturally without forcing, and balance between yin and yang, opposite forces like dark and light that need each other.

items: Each holds a seed of the other

explain.say: Confucius lived from 551 to 479 BCE. He was a teacher whose sayings his students gathered in the Analects. He taught ren, kindness and humanity, and li, proper conduct and respect.

items: 551 BCE: Confucius born in Lu, near Qufu

draw.a: Ren: humaneness. Li: right conduct and ritual.

explain.say: Confucius taught that society is harmonious when each relationship is kept with care, such as parent and child, ruler and people, and friend and friend. Respect for parents and ancestors is called filial piety.
In China, many people have long mixed these teachings with Buddhism, the three teachings. Confucius taught: do not do to others what you would not want done to yourself.

a: Follow the Tao, the way of nature

faq.a: Tao means the way. In Taoism it is the source and natural flow of the whole universe, beyond words. The Tao Te Ching begins by saying that the Tao that can be told is not the eternal Tao. Taoists try to live in harmony with it.
asks: What is the way in Taoism?

faq.a: Confucius taught that people become good through learning and practice, and society is peaceful when relationships are kept with respect. His key ideas are ren, humaneness, li, proper conduct, and filial piety, respect for parents and elders.

faq.q: What do yin and yang mean?
faq.a: Yin and yang are two opposite but connected forces, like dark and light, cool and warm, quiet and active. Neither is good or bad; harmony comes from their balance. The symbol shows each holding a small dot of the other.
asks: What is the yin yang symbol?

faq.a: Laozi, meaning old master, is the sage traditionally said to have written the Tao Te Ching, perhaps in the 500s BCE. Historians are not sure of the details of his life, and some think the book gathers wisdom from several authors.
asks: Who wrote the Tao Te Ching?

faq.q: What is the Tao Te Ching?
faq.a: The Tao Te Ching is the central Taoist book, about 81 short chapters of poetic wisdom on the Tao, nature, simplicity and gentle leadership. It is one of the most translated books in the world.
asks: What is the Taoist holy book?

faq.a: Wu wei means effortless action or not forcing. It does not mean doing nothing, but acting naturally and at the right time, like water flowing round a rock instead of fighting it.
Ren is the central Confucian virtue, often translated as humaneness, kindness or benevolence. It means caring for others and treating people well, starting with family and reaching out to all.
asks: What does ren mean in Confucianism?

faq.a: Li means ritual and proper conduct: the customs, manners and ceremonies that show respect, from greeting elders to honouring ancestors. Confucius believed practising li shapes good character.
Filial piety, xiao in Chinese, means love, respect and care for your parents and ancestors. Confucius saw it as the root of goodness, and it remains important in many East Asian families.

Scholars debate this. Confucianism is often described as a philosophy or ethical way of life, since it focuses on how to live and govern well. But it also includes rituals honouring ancestors and Confucius, so some call it a religion.
The Analects is a collection of the sayings and conversations of Confucius, gathered by his students after his death. It became one of the most important books in Chinese education.

faq.q: What are the three teachings of China?
faq.a: The three teachings are Confucianism, Taoism and Buddhism. Over many centuries in China, people often drew on all three: Confucian values at home, Taoist harmony with nature, and Buddhist practices.
asks: Can someone follow Taoism and Confucianism?

faq.q: What is the Confucian golden rule?
faq.a: In the Analects, Confucius says: do not do to others what you would not want done to yourself. It is a version of the golden rule found in many traditions.
asks: Did Confucius say the golden rule?

facts: Confucius lived from 551 to 479 BCE and came from the state of Lu, around Qufu in China.
The Analects collects the sayings of Confucius, gathered by his students.
The Tao Te Ching has 81 short chapters and is traditionally credited to Laozi.
Ren (humaneness), li (proper conduct) and xiao (filial piety) are key Confucian ideas.
Wu wei, effortless action, is a central Taoist idea.
